text:
Heill dagr, heilir dags synir,
heil nótt ok nipt.
meaning: "Hail, day! Hail, sons of day! And night and her daughter now!" (Henry Adams Bellows, 1936). The valkyrie Sigrdrífa’s greeting on waking, often called the oldest surviving Norse prayer.
purpose: To greet the day and the night with gratitude.
when: On waking, at dawn or at dusk.
note: From the Sigrdrífumál in the Poetic Edda. Its next lines hail the gods and goddesses and the bountiful earth.
source: Sigrdrífumál (Poetic Edda), Old Norse as normalised by Finnur Jónsson, 1932; translation Henry Adams Bellows, 1936
name: Hail, Day
iast:
Heill dagr, heilir dags synir,
heil nótt ok nipt.
pronunciation: hayl DAG-r, HAY-lir dags SIN-ir; hayl noht ok nipt
